equation_request.abstract: We apply our recent Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm [1] to the combinatorial problem of bounded occurrence Max E3LIN2. The input is a set of linear equations each of which contains exactly three boolean variables and each equation says that the sum of the variables mod 2 is 0 or is 1. Every variable is in no more than $D$ equations. A random string will satisfy 1/2 of the equations. We show that the level one QAOA will efficiently produce a string that satisfies $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{101D^{1/2}\,ln\,D}\right)$ times the number of equations. A recent classical algorithm [5, 6] achieved $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{constant}{D^{1/2}}\right)$. We also show that in the typical case the quantum computer will output a string that satisfies $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3e}\,D^{1/2}}\right)$ times the number of equations.

specification.problem: Bounded-occurrence Max E3LIN2: given m equations x_a+x_b+x_c = b (mod 2) over boolean variables, each variable in at most D equations, use level-one QAOA to output a string satisfying a fraction 1/2 + advantage of equations.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Define the E3LIN2 cost function, the level-one QAOA state and expectation objective, and the abstract's stated guarantees. Detailed level-one expectation formulas, the optimization of angles, and the proofs of the guarantees are outside scope. A tiny instance is not chosen beyond the generic form.

symbols.meaning: spin value of variable j, z_j = (-1)^{x_j}
maximum number of equations containing any variable
clause operator, equal to 1 if equation k is satisfied and 0 otherwise
total cost operator, the number of satisfied equations

equations.label: Clause operator
equations.description: Clause k is satisfied iff the parity of its three variables equals b_k, which is expressed through a product of Pauli Z operators.
equations.justification: The standard encoding of a mod-2 equation into a Z-product; the abstract only states the equation form.

equations.label: Level-one QAOA state
equations.description: Standard level-one QAOA state with a phase-separation step followed by a mixer step.
equations.justification: The abstract refers to a level-one QAOA but gives no explicit definition, so this is recalled standard form.

equations.label: Objective
equations.description: Expected number of satisfied equations, to be maximized over the angles.
equations.justification: Standard QAOA objective; the specific angle choice that gives the abstract's bounds is not reconstructed here.

equations.label: Worst-case guarantee
equations.description: Claimed satisfied fraction for level-one QAOA on bounded-occurrence instances.
equations.abstract_quote: We show that the level one QAOA will efficiently produce a string that satisfies $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{101D^{1/2}\,ln\,D}\right)$ times the number of equations.
equations.justification: Stated in the abstract. Whether it holds in expectation or with high probability is not specified, so the expectation form here is an interpretation.
assumptions: Interpreted as an expected or achievable fraction

equations.label: Typical-case guarantee
equations.abstract_quote: We also show that in the typical case the quantum computer will output a string that satisfies $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3e}\,D^{1/2}}\right)$ times the number of equations.
equations.justification: Stated in the abstract. The meaning of 'typical case' is not defined there.
assumptions: 'Typical case' is undefined in the abstract

registers.name: q
registers.role: one qubit per boolean variable, with qubit j encoding x_j in the computational basis

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition on n qubits.
Apply the phase-separation unitary exp(-i gamma C) built from the Z_aZ_bZ_c clause terms.
Apply the mixer exp(-i beta sum X_j).
Choose angles (gamma, beta) to meet the claimed guarantees; the specific values are not given in the abstract.

specification.measurement: Measure all qubits in the computational basis to obtain a candidate string x.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Count satisfied equations for the measured string and optionally repeat to keep the best string.
assumptions: Standard QAOA ansatz and Z-product clause encoding are assumed, not taken from the abstract.
